title: Pune-Hyderabad cloud kitchen cut Swiggy-Zomato dependence from 92% to 61% and doubled margin in 5 months
content: A 4-brand cloud kitchen across Pune and Hyderabad ran ~9,200 orders/month (₹41L GMV) with 92% flowing through Swiggy and Zomato. After 24-28% commission, in-app ad spend and forced discount-share, blended contribution margin was a brutal 9%, and direct app orders were under 8% — every reorder rented back at full take-rate. So we ran a 5-month own-the-reorder push. First, a QR sticker on every delivery bag and bill opened a branded WhatsApp + UPI ordering flow with a ₹75-off first-order code — far cheaper than the ₹130-150 margin we surrendered per aggregator order. Second, Meta and Instagram reorder retargeting (₹1.1L/month) hit past customers within 4km of each kitchen, AOV ₹340. Third, the kitchen WhatsApp line pushed a Tuesday-Thursday combo to repeat buyers on slow days. Over 5 months direct orders rose 8% to 39% of volume, aggregator dependence fell 92% to 61%, blended margin moved 9% to 19%, and direct-channel repeat rate hit 34% vs 11% on aggregators — lifting net monthly contribution by roughly ₹3.8L on a near-identical topline.
lesson: Aggregators win you the first order; you must win the reorder. Treat Swiggy and Zomato as paid acquisition, then put a direct-order QR on every bag and bribe the second order for less than the ₹130-150 commission you lose each time. Retention on an owned WhatsApp line — not louder in-app ads — is where a thin 9% margin becomes a survivable 19%.
